principle: General regulatory guidance defines evaluation and labeling structure; patient-level management still requires the current product label and applicable guideline unless an explicit product-specific rule is included here.

modules.title: Renal impairment dosing principle

source.title: Pharmacokinetics in Patients with Impaired Renal Function / Developing Dosage Recommendations

claims.claim: Dose recommendations in renal impairment should be based on the relationship among renal function, drug exposure, and exposure-response rather than on renal impairment alone.
claims.locator: Developing Dosage Recommendations in Patients with Impaired Renal Function

claims.claim: A change in pharmacokinetics with renal impairment does not automatically imply that a dose change is required for every drug.
claims.locator: Developing Dosage Recommendations in Patients with Impaired Renal Function

forbidden_inference: renal impairment -> automatic dose reduction for every drug
near a renal threshold -> treat as beyond the threshold

modules.title: Hepatic impairment PK/PD evaluation principle

source.title: Pharmacokinetics in Patients with Impaired Hepatic Function: Study Design, Data Analysis, and Impact on Dosing and Labeling

claims.claim: Hepatic impairment may alter a drug's PK and, where relevant, PD; dedicated evaluation can inform dosing and labeling.

forbidden_inference: hepatic impairment -> universal dose reduction
draft guidance -> patient-specific management rule

modules.title: Pregnancy labeling under PLLR

source.title: Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Final Rule

claims.claim: Prescription-drug pregnancy labeling uses narrative Risk Summary, Clinical Considerations, and Data rather than the former A/B/C/D/X pregnancy categories.
claims.locator: Pregnancy subsection 8.1 / removal of pregnancy letter categories

forbidden_inference: old pregnancy letter category -> current FDA risk classification
pregnancy exposure -> automatic contraindication without product-specific evidence

modules.title: Lactation labeling under PLLR

source.title: Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Final Rule

claims.claim: The Lactation subsection may address drug presence in human milk and potential effects on the breastfed infant, and must be interpreted product by product.

forbidden_inference: drug present in milk -> proven infant harm
no lactation data -> proven safety

modules.title: Females and males of reproductive potential

source.title: Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Final Rule

claims.claim: Label subsection 8.3 can include pregnancy testing, contraception recommendations, and infertility information when clinically relevant.
claims.locator: Females and Males of Reproductive Potential subsection 8.3

forbidden_inference: reproductive-potential warning -> pregnancy contraindication

modules.title: QTc labeling and concentration-dependent risk

source.title: QTc Information in Human Prescription Drug and Biological Product Labeling

claims.claim: Clinically relevant QTc information should be communicated in product labeling, including clinically significant prolongation, insufficient characterization, and relevant interaction contexts.

forbidden_inference: any QT signal -> torsades diagnosis
QT-related class membership -> identical risk across all drugs
general QT guidance -> product-specific stop rule

modules.title: Sertraline and serotonin syndrome

claims.claim: Sertraline can precipitate serotonin syndrome, and risk increases with concomitant serotonergic drugs or drugs that impair serotonin metabolism.
Serotonin-syndrome symptoms span mental-status, autonomic, neuromuscular, seizure, and gastrointestinal findings; no single nonspecific symptom alone establishes the syndrome.

forbidden_inference: one serotonergic symptom -> confirms serotonin syndrome
two serotonergic drugs -> patient definitely has serotonin syndrome

modules.title: Sulfonylurea severe hypoglycemia risk

claims.claim: Sulfonylureas including glipizide can produce severe hypoglycemia, and combination with other antidiabetic medication can increase hypoglycemia risk.

forbidden_inference: glipizide use -> current hypoglycemia diagnosis
risk factor -> confirmed event

modules.title: Acetaminophen severe liver-injury warning

claims.claim: The OTC label warns that severe liver damage may occur with more than 4,000 mg acetaminophen in 24 hours, with other acetaminophen-containing drugs, or with heavy daily alcohol use while taking the product.
claims.claim_scope: specific OTC acetaminophen 500 mg product warning

forbidden_inference: acetaminophen use -> DILI diagnosis
label warning -> incidence estimate
OTC product warning -> universal formulation-independent prescription rule

modules.title: Opioid-induced respiratory depression and naloxone reversal

claims.claim: Naloxone is indicated for complete or partial reversal of opioid depression including respiratory depression and for suspected or known acute opioid overdose.
Naloxone is not effective for respiratory depression caused by non-opioid drugs, so response to naloxone cannot be generalized to all causes of respiratory depression.
claims.locator: Respiratory Depression Due to Other Drugs

forbidden_inference: respiratory depression -> must be opioid toxicity
naloxone nonresponse -> rules out opioid exposure
